The reports therefore remain primary-searchable as proof metadata; ranking may demote this role behind authored formal-source hits, but the symbols must not be hidden by a physical or query-time .sys exclusion.

An exhaustive 2026-09-14 audit of the 9,359 nonempty reports found 589,709 distinct event identifiers that were absent from every retained non-.sys ACL2 source file under a conservative textual token check. These include generated contracts, induction schemes, signatures, accessors, and lemmas. The reports therefore remain primary-searchable as proof metadata; ranking may demote this role behind authored formal-source hits, but the symbols must not be hidden by a physical or query-time .sys exclusion.

title: Empty formal-source file

justification: ACL2 *@useless-runes.lsp files are certification-generated proof metadata, but generation does not make their searchable symbols redundant. An exhaustive 2026-09-14 audit of the 9,359 nonempty reports found 589,709 distinct event identifiers that were absent from every retained non-.sys ACL2 source file under a conservative textual token check. These include generated contracts, induction schemes, signatures, accessors, and lemmas. The reports therefore remain primary-searchable as proof metadata; ranking may demote this role behind authored formal-source hits, but the symbols must not be hidden by a physical or query-time .sys exclusion.

An exhaustive 2026-09-14 audit of the 9,359 nonempty reports found 589,709 distinct event identifiers that were absent from every retained non-.sys ACL2 source file under a conservative textual token check. These include generated contracts, induction schemes, signatures, accessors, and lemmas. The reports therefore remain primary-searchable as proof metadata; ranking may demote this role behind authored formal-source hits, but the symbols must not be hidden by a physical or query-time .sys exclusion.

The reports therefore remain primary-searchable as proof metadata; ranking may demote this role behind authored formal-source hits, but the symbols must not be hidden by a physical or query-time .sys exclusion.

These include generated contracts, induction schemes, signatures, accessors, and lemmas. The reports therefore remain primary-searchable as proof metadata; ranking may demote this role behind authored formal-source hits, but the symbols must not be hidden by a physical or query-time .sys exclusion.

An exhaustive 2026-09-14 audit of the 9,359 nonempty reports found 589,709 distinct event identifiers that were absent from every retained non-.sys ACL2 source file under a conservative textual token check. These include generated contracts, induction schemes, signatures, accessors, and lemmas. The reports therefore remain primary-searchable as proof metadata; ranking may demote this role behind authored formal-source hits, but the symbols must not be hidden by a physical or query-time .sys exclusion.

An exhaustive 2026-09-14 audit of the 9,359 nonempty reports found 589,709 distinct event identifiers that were absent from every retained non-.sys ACL2 source file under a conservative textual token check. These include generated contracts, induction schemes, signatures, accessors, and lemmas. The reports therefore remain primary-searchable as proof metadata; ranking may demote this role behind authored formal-source hits, but the symbols must not be hidden by a physical or query-time .sys exclusion.

An exhaustive 2026-09-14 audit of the 9,359 nonempty reports found 589,709 distinct event identifiers that were absent from every retained non-.sys ACL2 source file under a conservative textual token check. These include generated contracts, induction schemes, signatures, accessors, and lemmas. The reports therefore remain primary-searchable as proof metadata; ranking may demote this role behind authored formal-source hits, but the symbols must not be hidden by a physical or query-time .sys exclusion.

An exhaustive 2026-09-14 audit of the 9,359 nonempty reports found 589,709 distinct event identifiers that were absent from every retained non-.sys ACL2 source file under a conservative textual token check. These include generated contracts, induction schemes, signatures, accessors, and lemmas. The reports therefore remain primary-searchable as proof metadata; ranking may demote this role behind authored formal-source hits, but the symbols must not be hidden by a physical or query-time .sys exclusion.

justification: Byte-identical formal-source documents contain the same searchable file body, but their source and module paths are independent provenance and search signals. All occurrences therefore remain physically indexable for source/path queries. The public API collapses exact duplicate hits into one result and returns every occurrence as an alias. Physical content deduplication is deferred until alias paths can themselves participate in retrieval without loss.

All occurrences therefore remain physically indexable for source/path queries. The public API collapses exact duplicate hits into one result and returns every occurrence as an alias. Physical content deduplication is deferred until alias paths can themselves participate in retrieval without loss.

A formal Lean build script such as lakefile.lean is ordinary Lean source and is explicitly outside this decision: corpus audit found many such files containing definitions, structures, inductives, examples, and even axioms, so the filename alone cannot prove absence of useful formal prior art.

justification: Tree-sitter verification establishes that these Lean files own no declaration or proof, but that fact alone does not make their module names, paths, comments, provenance, or import topology dispensable search signals. FD-005 assumed those signals remained searchable through a deployed auxiliary navigation index. The production search service does not currently publish or query that index, so excluding these files from primary search violated FILTER-007's preservation requirement. Keep them in primary search, while also retaining the auxiliary copy, until an end-to-end searchable auxiliary channel is deployed and measured.

justification: README and source-documentation files outside the proof assistant's formal-source extensions can contain useful project terminology, provenance, references, and navigation, but they do not themselves constitute proof-assistant declarations or proofs. They are removed only from the primary mathematical-content index and retained in the auxiliary documentation/navigation index. A formal-source file such as README.lean, README.thy, README.agda, or Readme.lsp is never covered by this decision merely because of its basename.
title: Non-formal README or source documentation

justification: lean-toolchain, lake-manifest.json, and lakefile.toml are non-formal package/build metadata rather than proof-assistant source. They remain in the source checkout for reproducibility but are not fed to either mathematical or documentation search. A formal Lean build script such as lakefile.lean is ordinary Lean source and is explicitly outside this decision: corpus audit found many such files containing definitions, structures, inductives, examples, and even axioms, so the filename alone cannot prove absence of useful formal prior art.

They are removed only from the primary mathematical-content index and retained in the auxiliary documentation/navigation index. A formal-source file such as README.lean, README.thy, README.agda, or Readme.lsp is never covered by this decision merely because of its basename.

justification: lean-toolchain, lake-manifest.json, and lakefile.toml are non-formal package/build metadata rather than proof-assistant source. They remain in the source checkout for reproducibility but are not fed to either mathematical or documentation search. A formal Lean build script such as lakefile.lean is ordinary Lean source and is explicitly outside this decision: corpus audit found many such files containing definitions, structures, inductives, examples, and even axioms, so the filename alone cannot prove absence of useful formal prior art.
